role.en: Theologian and bishop of Hippo Regius

summary.en: Born to a Berber family in Roman Numidia, Augustine taught rhetoric in Carthage, Rome and Milan before his conversion. As bishop of Hippo for 35 years he wrote the Confessions and The City of God, shaping Western Christian thought; he died as the Vandals besieged his city.
summary.zh: 奥古斯丁出生于罗马努米底亚的柏柏尔家庭，曾在迦太基、罗马和米兰教授修辞学，后皈依基督教。他任希波主教35年，著有《忏悔录》和《上帝之城》，深刻影响西方基督教思想；在汪达尔人围城期间去世。

summary.en: Daughter of the mathematician Theon, Hypatia taught philosophy and mathematics in Alexandria and advised the city’s elite, pagan and Christian alike. Caught up in a feud between the prefect Orestes and Bishop Cyril, she was murdered by a Christian mob in 415.
summary.zh: 希帕提娅是数学家席昂之女，在亚历山大城讲授哲学与数学，为城中异教与基督教精英所敬重并充当顾问。她卷入总督奥瑞斯提斯与主教西里尔之争，415年遭基督徒暴民杀害。

label.en: Serapeum destroyed; she continues to teach
label.zh: 塞拉皮斯神庙被毁，她仍继续讲学

label.en: Leading teacher of Neoplatonism; pupils include Synesius
label.zh: 新柏拉图主义名师，学生包括辛奈西斯

label.en: Murdered by a mob during Lent
label.zh: 于大斋期间遭暴民杀害

note: Birth year uncertain (c. 350–370); Wikidata gives 360.

story.en:
Hypatia was the daughter of Theon, the last known mathematician attached to the Museum of Alexandria, and worked with him on editions of Ptolemy’s astronomy. Later sources credit her with commentaries on Diophantus’s Arithmetica and Apollonius’s Conics. She lectured publicly on Plato and Aristotle, wearing the philosopher’s cloak, and her pupils included Christians such as Synesius, later bishop of Ptolemais, whose surviving letters ask her to have a hydroscope made and who credited her teaching for an astrolabe he designed.

Her influence with the city’s elite drew her into politics. In 415 the imperial prefect Orestes was locked in a bitter feud with the patriarch Cyril, and rumours spread among Cyril’s supporters that Hypatia was blocking a reconciliation. According to the church historian Socrates Scholasticus, during Lent a crowd led by a church reader named Peter dragged her from her carriage, killed her inside the Caesareum church with potsherds and burned her remains.

Socrates, himself a Christian, condemned the murder as a disgrace to the church of Alexandria. Since the Enlightenment Hypatia has been retold, often freely, as a martyr of reason and a pioneer woman scientist.
story.zh:
希帕提娅是亚历山大博学园最后一位有记载的数学家塞翁之女，曾与父亲合作校订托勒密的天文学著作。后世文献称她为丢番图的《算术》和阿波罗尼奥斯的《圆锥曲线论》写过注释。她身披哲学家斗篷公开讲授柏拉图和亚里士多德，学生中也有基督徒，例如后来成为托勒迈斯主教的叙内修斯，他留存的书信请她代制一具比重计，他还把自己设计的星盘归功于她的教导。

她在城中上层的影响力把她卷入政治。415年，帝国长官奥瑞斯提斯与宗主教西里尔积怨甚深，西里尔的支持者中流传谣言，说是希帕提娅阻碍了双方和解。据教会史家苏格拉底·斯科拉斯提库斯记载，大斋期间，一群由教会诵经士彼得带领的人把她从马车上拖下，在凯撒利昂教堂里用陶片将她杀害，并焚烧了她的遗体。

本身是基督徒的苏格拉底谴责这场谋杀是亚历山大教会的耻辱。启蒙运动以来，希帕提娅的故事被反复改写（往往相当随意），她成了理性的殉道者和女性科学家的先驱。

summary.en: Ezana ruled Aksum at its height and became the first sub-Saharan monarch known to adopt Christianity. Trilingual inscriptions in Geʿez, Sabaean and Greek record his campaigns, including one against the Noba near Meroë. His birth and death years are unrecorded; the years shown are placeholders.
summary.zh: 埃扎纳在阿克苏姆鼎盛时期执政，是已知最早皈依基督教的撒哈拉以南君主。其吉兹语、萨巴语和希腊语三语铭文记载了他的征战，包括在麦罗埃附近对诺巴人的远征。其生卒年不见记载，此处所示年份仅为占位估计。

summary.en: A Lamtuna Sanhaja chief from the western Sahara, Yusuf built the Almoravid movement into an empire, founding Marrakesh and taking Fez. Invited by the taifa kings of al-Andalus, he defeated Alfonso VI at Sagrajas and then annexed Muslim Spain.
summary.zh: 优素福出身西撒哈拉的拉姆图纳·桑哈贾部落首领，将穆拉比特运动发展为帝国，建立马拉喀什并攻取非斯。他应安达卢斯诸泰法国王之请，在萨格拉哈斯击败阿方索六世，随后吞并穆斯林西班牙。

summary.en: Remembered in the griots’ epic as a disabled child who rose to free the Mande from Sosso domination, Sundiata defeated Sumanguru at Kirina and founded the Mali Empire. Ibn Khaldun, writing a century later, records him as Mari Jata.
summary.zh: 在格里奥史诗中，松迪亚塔幼年残疾，后崛起将曼丁人从索索统治下解放。他在基里纳击败苏曼古鲁，建立马里帝国。一个世纪后，伊本·赫勒敦以“马里·贾塔”之名记载了他。

label.zh: 生于曼丁（传统认为在尼亚尼）

story.en:
In the Sunjata epic sung by Mande griots, Sundiata is the son of the king of Manding and Sogolon, a hunchbacked woman foretold to bear a great ruler. As a child he cannot walk, and his father’s senior wife mocks his mother. Stung by an insult, the boy calls for an iron rod, which bends into a bow as he hauls himself upright; in some versions he then uproots a baobab and lays it at his mother’s door.

Forced into exile by his half-brother’s faction, he grows up at distant courts, including Mema, where he wins renown as a hunter and warrior. When Sumanguru of Sosso conquers Manding, envoys find him and bring him home to lead the allied clans to victory at Kirina.

These episodes are tradition, not documented history, and they vary from village to village. The written record is thin: Ibn Khaldun names a king Mari Jata who conquered Sosso and ruled for about twenty-five years. Every seven years the Kamabolon sanctuary at Kangaba is re-roofed while griots of the Diabaté family recite the epic, a ceremony UNESCO lists as intangible heritage.
story.zh:
在曼丁格格里奥传唱的《松迪亚塔史诗》中，松迪亚塔是曼丁国王与驼背女子索戈隆之子，预言称她将生下一位伟大的君主。他幼时不能行走，父亲的正妻常常嘲笑他的母亲。一次受辱之后，男孩要来一根铁棒，撑着它站起来时铁棒弯成了弓；有些版本说他随即拔起一棵猴面包树，放到母亲门前。

他被同父异母兄长的一派逼迫流亡，在远方的宫廷长大，其中包括梅马，在那里以猎人和武士闻名。苏曼古鲁征服曼丁后，使者找到他并把他接回，由他率领联合各族在基里纳取胜。

这些情节属于口头传统而非有据可查的历史，各村说法不一。文字记载很少：伊本·赫勒敦提到一位名叫马里·贾塔的国王征服了索索，在位约二十五年。在康加巴，每七年为卡马博隆圣所重铺屋顶，届时迪亚巴特家族的格里奥吟诵史诗，这一仪式已被联合国教科文组织列为非物质文化遗产。

summary.en: Ruler of Mali at its greatest extent, Musa made a celebrated pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324–1325, displaying such wealth in Cairo that Arab writers recalled it for decades. He annexed Gao and Timbuktu and patronised mosques and scholars, establishing Timbuktu as a centre of learning.
summary.zh: 穆萨统治时马里疆域最为辽阔，1324–1325年赴麦加朝觐，在开罗显示的财富令阿拉伯作家数十年津津乐道。他兼并加奥和廷巴克图，资助清真寺与学者，使廷巴克图成为学术中心。

label.zh: 下令修建津加雷贝尔清真寺

sources.title: al-ʿUmari, Masalik al-Absar, in Levtzion & Hopkins, Corpus
al-Sa'di, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (2003)
Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)
N. Levtzion and J. F. P. Hopkins (eds.), Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981): al-ʿUmari, Masalik al-absar

note: Reign dates vary (1312–1337 per Ibn Khaldun’s chronology; some give 1307–1332).

story.en:
Musa explained his own accession to the officials of Cairo, and the scholar al-ʿUmari recorded the account. His predecessor, he said, refused to believe that the Atlantic had no far shore and sent out two hundred ships; only one returned, reporting that the others had vanished in a current far out at sea. The king then set out himself with two thousand vessels, leaving Musa as regent, and was never seen again. Historians treat the story with caution, but it is the only medieval report of such a voyage from West Africa.

Musa’s reign was the high point of Mali. His generals brought Gao and the Songhai under Malian rule, and Timbuktu grew into a centre of trade and Islamic learning, with new mosques attributed to the architect al-Sahili. He exchanged embassies with the Marinid sultan of Morocco and was remembered across the Muslim world as a pious and lavish king.

Ibn Khaldun, writing later in the century, preserved Malian traditions about him from informants at the Marinid court. Mali remained powerful under his brother Sulayman, but began to lose its eastern provinces within a few decades.
story.zh:
穆萨曾向开罗官员讲述自己继位的经过，学者乌马里记下了这番话。他说，前任国王不相信大西洋没有彼岸，派出两百艘船；只有一艘返回，报告说其余船只在远海的一股洋流中消失。国王于是亲率两千艘船出海，留穆萨摄政，从此一去不返。史家对这一说法持审慎态度，但它是中世纪唯一一份关于西非有过此类航行的记载。

穆萨在位时期是马里的鼎盛时代。他的将领把加奥和桑海人纳入马里统治，廷巴克图发展为商业和伊斯兰学术中心，新建的清真寺据说出自建筑师萨赫利之手。他与摩洛哥马林王朝苏丹互派使节，在整个穆斯林世界被铭记为一位虔诚而慷慨的君主。

同世纪稍晚写作的伊本·赫勒敦，从马林王朝宫廷的消息提供者那里保存了有关他的马里传说。在其弟苏莱曼治下，马里依然强盛，但几十年内便开始失去东部诸省。

summary.en: A Berber jurist from Tangier, Ibn Battuta travelled for nearly thirty years through the Islamic world and beyond, from the Swahili coast to China. His Rihla, dictated in Fez, includes the only eyewitness description of the court of Mali under Mansa Sulayman (1352–1353).
summary.zh: 丹吉尔的柏柏尔法学家伊本·白图泰游历伊斯兰世界及更远地区近三十年，足迹从斯瓦希里海岸直至中国。他在非斯口述的《游记》包含唯一一份亲历马里曼萨苏莱曼宫廷（1352–1353年）的记载。

story.en:
Ibn Battuta left Tangier at twenty-one to make the pilgrimage to Mecca and kept travelling for most of the next three decades, by his own account covering lands from the Volga to the Swahili coast and from Delhi to China. The historian Ross Dunn estimates his journeys at some 117,000 kilometres. In Delhi the sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq made him a judge and later sent him as envoy to China, a mission that began with shipwreck.

His last great journey took him across the Sahara in 1352. At the salt-mining town of Taghaza he saw houses built of salt; at the court of Mansa Sulayman of Mali he was disappointed by the king’s welcome gift of bread, fried beef and a gourd of soured milk, and he laughed at its meanness. Yet he praised the Malians’ devotion to prayer and the safety of travel in their country, even as he disapproved of women’s freedom of dress and company.

Back in Fez, the Marinid sultan had the scholar Ibn Juzayy write down his memories as the Rihla. Some readers doubted his tales then, and modern scholars suspect a few sections were borrowed from earlier writers.
story.zh:
伊本·白图泰二十一岁离开丹吉尔前往麦加朝觐，此后近三十年大多在旅途中度过。据他自述，足迹从伏尔加河到斯瓦希里海岸，从德里到中国。史家罗斯·邓恩估计他的行程约达11.7万公里。在德里，苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克任命他为法官，后又派他出使中国，这次出使以海难开场。

他最后一次远行是1352年穿越撒哈拉。在产盐的塔加扎，他看到用盐块砌成的房屋；在马里曼萨苏莱曼的宫廷，国王赐予的见面礼只有面包、炸牛肉和一葫芦酸奶，令他大失所望，忍不住笑其吝啬。但他也称赞马里人虔诚礼拜，境内旅行安全，同时对当地妇女着装与交往的自由颇有微词。

回到非斯后，马林王朝苏丹命学者伊本·朱扎伊把他的回忆笔录成《游记》。当时已有人怀疑他的故事，现代学者也认为其中少数段落可能借自前人著作。

summary.en: Born in Hafsid Tunis to an Andalusi family, Ibn Khaldun served several North African and Granadan courts before writing the Muqaddimah and his universal history. He spent his last decades in Mamluk Cairo as a Maliki judge and met Timur outside Damascus in 1401.
summary.zh: 伊本·赫勒敦生于哈夫斯王朝治下突尼斯的安达卢斯家族，先后效力于北非诸王廷和格拉纳达，之后写成《历史绪论》及通史。晚年数十年在马穆鲁克开罗任马利克派法官，1401年在大马士革城外会见帖木儿。

summary.en: A Soninke general under Sonni Ali, Muhammad Ture seized the Songhai throne at Anfao in 1493 and founded the Askia dynasty. He reorganised the empire’s provinces and army, made the hajj, was named caliph for the western Sudan, and extended Songhai rule from the Atlantic hinterland to Hausaland.

summary.en: Born in Granada and raised in Fez, al-Hasan al-Wazzan travelled as a Moroccan envoy to Timbuktu and Egypt. Captured by Christian corsairs, he was baptised by Pope Leo X and wrote the Description of Africa, Europe’s main source on the African interior for two centuries.

summary.en: The most celebrated scholar of Timbuktu, Ahmad Baba wrote some forty works on law, grammar and biography. After the Moroccan conquest he was deported in chains to Marrakesh, where he taught; his treatise on slavery argued against enslaving Muslims.
summary.zh: 艾哈迈德·巴巴是廷巴克图最负盛名的学者，著有约四十部法学、语法和传记著作。摩洛哥征服后，他被锁押至马拉喀什，在那里讲学；其论奴隶制的著作反对奴役穆斯林。

label.zh: 摩洛哥征服后被押往马拉喀什

name.zh: 恩东戈与马坦巴女王恩津加

summary.en: Njinga Mbande negotiated with the Portuguese in Luanda in 1622, then ruled Ndongo and conquered Matamba. For three decades she fought Portuguese expansion through war, alliances with the Dutch and Imbangala, and diplomacy, securing a peace treaty in 1657.
summary.zh: 恩津加·姆班德于1622年在罗安达与葡萄牙人谈判，随后统治恩东戈并征服马坦巴。三十年间她以战争、与荷兰人和因班加拉人结盟以及外交手段抵抗葡萄牙扩张，于1657年取得和约。

label.en: Born at the Ndongo court (Kabasa, approx.)
label.zh: 生于恩东戈王廷（卡巴萨，约略）

label.en: Embassy to the Portuguese governor in Luanda; baptised Ana
label.zh: 出使罗安达葡萄牙总督，受洗名安娜

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba
Linda M. Heywood, Njinga of Angola: Africa’s Warrior Queen (2017)
Giovanni Antonio Cavazzi, Istorica descrizione de’ tre regni Congo, Matamba et Angola (1687)

note: Inland locations (Kabasa, Matamba) are approximate.

story.en:
In 1622 Njinga’s brother, the Ngola Mbandi, sent her to Luanda to negotiate with the Portuguese governor João Correia de Sousa. According to the Capuchin missionary Cavazzi, the governor received her seated on a chair while offering her only a mat on the floor; at a sign, one of her attendants knelt, and Njinga sat on the woman’s back to talk with him as an equal. She agreed to be baptised as Ana de Sousa and won a treaty, which the Portuguese soon ignored.

After Mbandi’s death in 1624 she claimed power in Ndongo, though many nobles rejected a woman ruler. Driven from her lands, she allied with the Imbangala warbands, adopting their military rites, and seized the kingdom of Matamba as a new base. During the Dutch occupation of Luanda (1641–48) she fought beside the Dutch and nearly drove the Portuguese from the interior.

In 1657, in her seventies, she made peace with Portugal, recovering her captive sister Barbara. She died in 1663 and is honoured in Angola as a symbol of resistance, with a statue in Luanda.
story.zh:
1622年，恩津加的兄长恩戈拉·姆班迪派她前往罗安达，与葡萄牙总督若昂·科雷亚·德·索萨谈判。据嘉布遣会传教士卡瓦齐记载，总督坐在椅子上接见她，却只给她地上铺一张席子；她一示意，一名侍女便跪伏下来，恩津加坐在侍女背上与总督平起平坐地交谈。她同意受洗，取名安娜·德·索萨，并争取到一项条约，但葡萄牙人很快便置之不理。

1624年姆班迪死后，她宣布执掌恩东戈，但许多贵族不承认女性统治者。她被逐出领地后，与因班加拉武装集团结盟，采纳其军事仪规，并夺取马坦巴王国作为新的根据地。荷兰占领罗安达期间（1641—1648年），她与荷兰人并肩作战，几乎把葡萄牙人逐出内陆。

1657年，年逾七旬的她与葡萄牙议和，赎回了被俘的妹妹芭芭拉。她于1663年去世，在安哥拉被尊为抵抗的象征，罗安达立有她的雕像。

name.zh: 多娜·贝亚特丽斯·金帕·维塔

role.en: Prophet of the Antonian movement in Kongo
role.zh: 刚果安东尼派运动女先知

summary.en: A young Kongolese noblewoman, Kimpa Vita declared herself possessed by Saint Anthony and preached an Africanised Catholicism, urging the reunification of the war-torn kingdom. Her followers reoccupied the ruined capital São Salvador before King Pedro IV had her burned as a heretic.
summary.zh: 刚果年轻贵族女子金帕·维塔宣称圣安东尼附身，宣讲本土化的天主教，呼吁饱受战乱的王国重新统一。她的追随者重新占据已成废墟的首都圣萨尔瓦多，后国王佩德罗四世以异端罪将她处以火刑。

label.zh: 生于基班古山附近（约略）
追随者重占圣萨尔瓦多（姆班扎刚果）

label.en: Burned at Evululu on Pedro IV’s orders
label.zh: 奉佩德罗四世之命在埃武卢卢被处火刑

sources.title: John K. Thornton, The Kongolese Saint Anthony: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita and the Antonian Movement (1998)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)
John K. Thornton, The Kongolese Saint Anthony: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita and the Antonian Movement, 1684–1706 (1998)

note: Kibangu and Evululu positions are approximate.

story.en:
By 1700 the kingdom of Kongo had been torn apart for decades by rival claimants, and its capital, São Salvador, lay in ruins. In 1704 a young noblewoman named Beatriz Kimpa Vita fell gravely ill and recovered declaring that Saint Anthony of Padua had entered her body. She began to preach, first at the court of King Pedro IV at Kibangu, that God was angered by the civil wars and wanted the capital reoccupied.

Her Antonian movement taught that Jesus, Mary and Saint Francis had been Kongolese, replaced the Salve Regina with a prayer called the Salve Antoniana, and attacked both old charms and the crucifixes that Italian Capuchin missionaries promoted. Thousands of followers resettled São Salvador, and she backed a rival claimant to the throne.

In 1706 she gave birth to a son, which damaged her claims to holiness, and Pedro IV’s men captured her with her companion João Barro. Accused of heresy on evidence given by the Capuchin Bernardo da Gallo, she was burned at Evululu on 2 July 1706. Pedro restored the capital in 1709, partly fulfilling her call for reunification.
story.zh:
到1700年，刚果王国已因各派争夺王位而分裂数十年，都城圣萨尔瓦多沦为废墟。1704年，年轻的贵族女子贝亚特丽丝·金帕·维塔身患重病，康复后宣称帕多瓦的圣安东尼附在了她身上。她开始传道，最初是在基邦古的国王佩德罗四世宫廷，说上帝对内战震怒，要求人们重新占据都城。

她的“安东尼运动”宣称耶稣、马利亚和圣方济各都是刚果人，用名为《安东尼颂》的祷文取代《圣母颂》，既抨击旧有的护符，也抨击意大利嘉布遣会传教士推广的十字架苦像。数千名追随者重新定居圣萨尔瓦多，她还支持了另一位王位争夺者。

1706年她生下一子，这损害了她自称圣洁的声望；佩德罗四世的部下将她和同伴若昂·巴罗一同抓获。根据嘉布遣会士贝尔纳多·达·加洛提供的证词，她被控为异端，于1706年7月2日在埃武卢卢被处以火刑。佩德罗于1709年恢复了都城，在某种程度上实现了她统一王国的呼吁。

summary.en: A Fulani scholar of the Qadiriyya order, Usman dan Fodio preached reform in Hausaland for thirty years before leading the jihad of 1804. He wrote over a hundred works in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa and left the administration of the new caliphate to his son Muhammad Bello and brother Abdullahi.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥是卡迪里教团的富拉尼学者，在豪萨地区宣讲改革三十年后，于1804年领导圣战。他以阿拉伯语、富拉语和豪萨语写下百余部著作，将新哈里发国的治理交给儿子穆罕默德·贝洛和兄弟阿卜杜拉希。

summary.en: Trained in the army of the Mthethwa paramount Dingiswayo, Shaka took over the small Zulu chiefdom in 1816 and, through age-regiments and new close-combat tactics, forged a powerful centralised kingdom. He was assassinated by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana in 1828.
summary.zh: 恰卡曾在姆特特瓦首领丁吉斯瓦约麾下受训，1816年接掌弱小的祖鲁酋邦，凭借年龄兵团与新的近战战术建立起强大的中央集权王国。1828年被同父异母兄弟丁冈与姆兰加纳刺杀。

label.zh: 在姆拉图泽河击败恩德万德人（约略）

sources.title: Carolyn Hamilton, Terrific Majesty: The Powers of Shaka Zulu and the Limits of Historical Invention (1998)
Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

note: Birth year approximate; early-life sites known only approximately.

story.en:
Shaka was born to the Zulu chief Senzangakhona and Nandi of the Langeni, and tradition says the boy and his mother were driven out and spent a hard childhood among other clans. He made his name as a warrior in the regiments of Dingiswayo of the Mthethwa, who helped him seize the Zulu chieftaincy around 1816.

Zulu tradition credits him with reorganising warfare: age-regiments housed in royal homesteads, the short stabbing spear (the iklwa) used with a large cowhide shield at close quarters, and the encircling “horns of the buffalo”. After defeating the Ndwandwe he ruled a kingdom covering much of present-day KwaZulu-Natal, and the wars of the period displaced many neighbouring peoples, although historians now debate how far the upheavals called the Mfecane were his doing.

English traders who settled at Port Natal in 1824, among them Henry Francis Fynn, left accounts of his court that are vivid but self-serving. They describe mass killings in the mourning that followed Nandi’s death in 1827. In September 1828 his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana stabbed him to death at KwaDukuza.
story.zh:
沙卡是祖鲁酋长森赞格科纳与兰格尼部女子南迪之子。据传说，母子二人被逐出部落，在其他氏族中度过了艰难的童年。他在姆塞特瓦部首领丁吉斯瓦约的军团中以勇武成名，约1816年在丁吉斯瓦约的帮助下夺得祖鲁酋长之位。

祖鲁传统把军事改革归功于他：按年龄编组、驻扎在王家营地的军团，近战时配合大牛皮盾使用的短刺矛“伊克瓦”，以及包抄敌人的“水牛角”阵型。击败恩德万德人后，他统治的王国覆盖今夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省大部分地区；这一时期的战争使许多邻近民族流离失所，不过所谓“姆菲卡尼”动荡在多大程度上由他造成，史学界至今仍有争论。

1824年定居纳塔尔港的英国商人（其中有亨利·弗朗西斯·芬恩）留下了关于其宫廷的记述，生动却带有私心。他们描述了1827年南迪去世后服丧期间的大规模杀戮。1828年9月，他的同父异母兄弟丁冈和姆兰加纳在夸杜库扎将他刺死。

summary.en: An Albanian officer sent against the French, Muhammad Ali seized power in Egypt, destroyed the Mamluk elite and built a conscript army, state monopolies and factories. His campaigns reached Arabia, Sudan and Syria, and his dynasty ruled Egypt until the monarchy was abolished in 1953.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里原为奉派抗击法军的阿尔巴尼亚军官，夺取埃及政权后消灭马穆鲁克精英，建立征兵制军队、国家专营和工厂。其征战远及阿拉伯半岛、苏丹和叙利亚，他的王朝统治埃及，直至1953年君主制被废除。

summary.en: King of Shewa from 1865 and emperor from 1889, Menelik expanded Ethiopia south and west to roughly its modern borders, founded Addis Ababa with Empress Taytu, and defeated Italy at Adwa. He introduced railways, telegraphs and modern schools.
summary.zh: 孟尼利克1865年起为绍阿国王，1889年称帝，将埃塞俄比亚向南、向西扩张至大致今日的疆界，与泰图皇后共建亚的斯亚贝巴，并在阿杜瓦击败意大利。他引入了铁路、电报和现代学校。

label.zh: 生于绍阿的安戈拉拉（约略）

label.en: Held at Magdala by Tewodros II
label.zh: 被特沃德罗斯二世扣押于马格达拉

label.en: Escapes; King of Shewa at Ankober
label.zh: 出逃，在安科伯为绍阿国王

sources.title: Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Harold G. Marcus, The Life and Times of Menelik II: Ethiopia 1844–1913 (1975)

story.en:
As a boy Menelik, heir to the kingdom of Shewa, was captured by Emperor Tewodros II and held at the mountain fortress of Magdala. Tewodros treated him almost as a son and married him to his daughter Altash, but in 1865 Menelik escaped and returned to claim Shewa. While Tewodros fell to the British and Yohannes IV ruled as emperor, Menelik built up his power, buying rifles from European merchants and conquering the Oromo, Gurage and Sidama lands to the south.

On Yohannes’s death in 1889 he became emperor. The same year he signed the Treaty of Wuchale with Italy, whose disputed clause led to war and to his victory at Adwa in 1896. Afterwards he pushed Ethiopia’s frontiers to roughly their present shape and negotiated borders with Britain, France and Italy.

In his new capital, Addis Ababa, he brought in eucalyptus trees to ease a firewood shortage that threatened to force the court to move again, and approved the railway to Djibouti, telephones and the first modern school and bank. Strokes incapacitated him from 1908, and when he died in December 1913 his death was kept secret for a time.
story.zh:
孟尼利克作为绍阿王国的继承人，少年时被皇帝特沃德罗斯二世俘获，关押在马格达拉山寨。特沃德罗斯待他几乎如同己出，还把女儿阿尔塔什嫁给他，但1865年孟尼利克逃脱，回到绍阿称王。当特沃德罗斯败于英军、约翰尼斯四世称帝之时，孟尼利克积蓄实力，向欧洲商人购买步枪，征服了南方的奥罗莫、古拉格和锡达玛地区。

1889年约翰尼斯去世，他继位为皇帝。同年他与意大利签订《乌查利条约》，其中有争议的条款引发战争，最终使他在1896年赢得阿杜瓦大捷。此后他把埃塞俄比亚疆域扩展到大致今天的范围，并与英、法、意三国议定边界。

在新都亚的斯亚贝巴，他引种桉树以缓解薪柴短缺，否则朝廷可能不得不再次迁都；他还批准修建通往吉布提的铁路，引进电话，创办第一所现代学校和第一家银行。1908年起他因中风丧失理政能力，1913年12月去世时，死讯曾被秘而不宣一段时间。

summary.en: Of noble Semien and Yejju descent, Taytu married Menelik in 1883 and became one of the most powerful figures at court. She chose the site of Addis Ababa, opposed the Treaty of Wuchale, commanded troops at Adwa, and effectively governed during Menelik’s final illness.
summary.zh: 泰图出身塞米恩与耶居贵族，1883年嫁给孟尼利克，成为宫廷中最有权势的人物之一。她选定亚的斯亚贝巴的城址，反对《乌查利条约》，在阿杜瓦指挥军队，并在孟尼利克病重期间实际执政。

在安科伯嫁给孟尼利克

label.zh: 选定温泉之地建亚的斯亚贝巴

sources.title: Chris Prouty, Empress Taytu and Menilek II: Ethiopia 1883–1910 (1986)
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)

note: Birth year and birthplace vary between sources.

story.en:
Taytu Betul had been married several times before she wed Menelik of Shewa in 1883, and she brought him the support of powerful northern noble families. She was literate in Ge’ez, played the begena lyre and composed poetry, and quickly became his most trusted political adviser.

She distrusted the Italians from the start and was among the fiercest opponents of the Treaty of Wuchale. In the campaign of 1895–96 she marched with her own troops. During the siege of the Italian fort at Mekelle in January 1896 she is credited with the idea of seizing the springs that supplied its water, forcing the garrison to negotiate its withdrawal. At Adwa she commanded a contingent of several thousand and directed women carrying water to the front.

In Addis Ababa, whose hot-springs site she had chosen, she founded the city’s first hotel. As Menelik declined after 1908 she ruled in his name and advanced her relatives, until in 1910 a coalition of Shewan nobles forced her from power. She spent her last years at Entoto, where she died in 1918.
story.zh:
泰图·贝图尔在1883年嫁给绍阿国王孟尼利克之前已有过数次婚姻，她为孟尼利克带来了北方显赫贵族家族的支持。她通晓吉兹文，会弹奏贝格纳竖琴并写作诗歌，很快成为他最信任的政治顾问。

她从一开始就不信任意大利人，是《乌查利条约》最激烈的反对者之一。在1895—1896年的战役中，她率领自己的部队随军出征。1896年1月围攻意大利梅克莱要塞时，据说是她提出夺取为要塞供水的泉眼，迫使守军谈判撤离。在阿杜瓦，她指挥一支数千人的队伍，并组织妇女为前线运水。

在她亲自选定温泉地址的亚的斯亚贝巴，她创办了城里第一家旅馆。1908年后孟尼利克病重，她以他的名义执政并提拔亲属，直到1910年绍阿贵族联合起来迫使她交出权力。她晚年住在恩托托，1918年在那里去世。

summary.en: A Maninka trader turned military leader, Samori built the Wassoulou state with a disciplined army armed with imported breech-loading and repeating rifles, plus copies made by his own smiths. He resisted French conquest for nearly two decades, relocating his whole state eastward, until his capture in 1898.
summary.zh: 萨摩里原为马林凯商人，后成为军事领袖，建立瓦苏卢国家，其纪律严明的军队装备进口的后膛枪和连发步枪，并有自家铁匠仿制的枪支。他抵抗法国征服近二十年，甚至将整个国家东迁，直至1898年被俘。

story.en:
Born Rolihlahla into a Thembu royal family, he was given the name Nelson by a teacher on his first day at school. Expelled from Fort Hare after a student protest, he fled an arranged marriage to Johannesburg, qualified in law and in 1952 opened South Africa’s first Black law partnership with Oliver Tambo. After the Sharpeville massacre and the banning of the ANC in 1960 he helped found the armed wing Umkhonto we Sizwe and went underground.

At the Rivonia trial in April 1964 he ended a three-hour statement from the dock by saying that a free, democratic society was an ideal for which he was prepared to die. He spent eighteen of his twenty-seven years in prison on Robben Island as prisoner 466/64, breaking limestone in a quarry whose glare damaged his eyes, while “Free Mandela” became a worldwide slogan.

Released on 11 February 1990, he negotiated with F. W. de Klerk, with whom he shared the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize. As president he wore a Springbok jersey to present the 1995 Rugby World Cup to the mostly white team, a gesture of reconciliation, and stepped down after one term.
story.zh:
他出生于滕布王族，本名罗利赫拉赫拉，上学第一天老师给他取名纳尔逊。他因参加学生抗议被黑尔堡大学开除，为逃避包办婚姻来到约翰内斯堡，取得律师资格，1952年与奥利弗·坦博合开南非第一家黑人律师事务所。1960年沙佩维尔惨案发生、非国大被取缔后，他参与创建武装组织“民族之矛”并转入地下。

1964年4月的里沃尼亚审判中，他在被告席上作了三小时陈述，最后表示，一个自由民主的社会是他愿意为之献身的理想。在二十七年的牢狱生涯中，他有十八年以466/64号囚犯的身份关押在罗本岛，在采石场敲打石灰石，刺目的反光损伤了他的眼睛；与此同时，“释放曼德拉”成为响彻全球的口号。

1990年2月11日获释后，他与德克勒克谈判，二人共获1993年诺贝尔和平奖。担任总统期间，他身穿跳羚队球衣为以白人为主的南非队颁发1995年橄榄球世界杯奖杯，以此表达和解之意；他只任一届便卸任。

note: Her life is known only from Arabic sources written centuries later; the birth year is a placeholder and her death is dated 698–703 in different sources.

story.en:
Almost everything about Dihya is contested, including her name and her religion. The Arab historians who wrote about her, the earliest two centuries after her death, call her al-Kahina, the prophetess or soothsayer, and say she led the Jarawa tribe of the Aurès mountains in what is now eastern Algeria. Ibn Khaldun reports that some said her people were Jewish; others make her Christian or pagan.

After the Arabs took Carthage in the 690s, she became the leader of Berber resistance. Near the Meskiana river she routed the army of Hassan ibn al-Nuʿman and drove it back to Tripolitania. According to the chronicles she then ordered a scorched-earth policy, cutting down orchards and destroying towns so that the invaders would find nothing worth taking, which turned many settled people against her.

When Hassan returned with reinforcements, she was defeated and killed, by tradition at a well that still bears her name. The chronicles say she had told her sons to join the Arabs, and they commanded Berber troops in the conquest. Since the colonial era she has been claimed as a heroine by Berber activists, Algerian nationalists and French writers alike.
story.zh:
关于迪希亚的几乎一切都有争议，包括她的名字和宗教。记述她的阿拉伯史家最早也在她死后两个世纪才写作，称她为“卡希娜”（女先知或占卜者），说她领导今阿尔及利亚东部奥雷斯山区的贾拉瓦部落。伊本·赫勒敦记载，有人说她的族人是犹太人；另一些人则说她是基督徒或异教徒。

7世纪90年代阿拉伯人攻占迦太基后，她成为柏柏尔人抵抗的领袖。她在梅斯基亚纳河附近击溃哈桑·本·努曼的军队，把他赶回的黎波里塔尼亚。据编年史记载，她随后下令实行焦土政策，砍伐果园、摧毁城镇，使入侵者一无所获，这让许多定居民众转而反对她。

哈桑带着援军卷土重来，她兵败被杀，传说死在一口至今以她命名的井边。编年史称她曾嘱咐儿子们投奔阿拉伯人，后来他们在征服中统领柏柏尔军队。殖民时代以来，柏柏尔活动人士、阿尔及利亚民族主义者和法国作家都把她奉为女英雄。

story.en:
Idris Alooma is the best-documented African king of the 16th century outside Ethiopia because his imam, Ahmad ibn Furtu, wrote a detailed account of his first twelve years of campaigns. Ibn Furtu describes a king who studied the Quran, built mosques of burnt brick, appointed qadis and made the pilgrimage to Mecca early in his reign.

He was also an innovator in war. He bought firearms through the trade with Ottoman Tripoli and employed Turkish musketeers, used camels to move supplies, and made his army fortify its camp every night with a stockade. The siege of Amsaka, a walled town south of Lake Chad, shows his methods: his men built an earth ramp up to the walls and fired down into the town until it fell.

He died, according to tradition, at Alau, near modern Maiduguri, struck by a hidden enemy while he was in the fields. Under him and his successors Bornu controlled the trade routes from Lake Chad north to the Fezzan and remained one of the great powers of the Sahel until the 19th century.
story.zh:
伊德里斯·阿卢马是16世纪埃塞俄比亚以外记载最详细的非洲国王，因为他的伊玛目艾哈迈德·本·富尔图详细记述了他头十二年的征战。富尔图笔下的国王研读《古兰经》，用烧砖修建清真寺，任命卡迪（法官），并在即位初期前往麦加朝觐。

他也是军事革新者。他通过与奥斯曼属的黎波里的贸易购买火器，雇用土耳其火枪手，用骆驼运送补给，并要求军队每晚以木栅加固营地。对乍得湖以南有城墙的阿姆萨卡的围攻展示了他的战法：士兵们筑起通向城墙的土坡，居高临下向城内射击，直至城破。

据传说，他在今迈杜古里附近的阿劳田间被暗藏的敌人击中身亡。在他和继任者治下，博尔努控制着从乍得湖向北通往费赞的商道，直到19世纪仍是萨赫勒地区的强国之一。

summary.en: Called Gragn, “the left-handed”, in Amharic, Imam Ahmad united the Somali and Afar forces of Adal, defeated Emperor Lebna Dengel at Shimbra Kure in 1529 and overran most of the Christian highlands. He was killed at Wayna Daga in 1543 by an Ethiopian–Portuguese army.
summary.zh: 阿姆哈拉语称他为“格兰”（左撇子）。伊玛目艾哈迈德统一了阿达勒的索马里人和阿法尔人力量，1529年在欣布拉库雷击败皇帝莱布纳·登格尔，占领了基督教高原的大部分地区。1543年他在瓦伊纳达加被埃塞俄比亚与葡萄牙联军击毙。

label.en: Born in the Hubat region near Harar
label.zh: 生于哈勒尔附近的胡巴特地区

label.en: Takes power in Harar and proclaims jihad
label.zh: 在哈勒尔掌权并宣布圣战
兵抵提格雷的阿克苏姆

label.en: Killed at Wayna Daga near Lake Tana
label.zh: 在塔纳湖附近的瓦伊纳达加阵亡

sources.title: Shihab al-Din Arabfaqih, Futuh al-Habasha, trans. Paul Lester Stenhouse (2003)

note: Birth year approximate; battlefield locations approximate.

role.en: First Asantehene, founder of the Asante Empire
role.zh: 首任阿散蒂赫内（阿散蒂国王），阿散蒂帝国创建者

summary.en: Raised at the courts of Denkyira and Akwamu, Osei Tutu united the Akan chiefdoms around Kumasi into a confederacy, with the priest Okomfo Anokye, and broke Denkyira’s power at Feyiase in 1701. The Golden Stool, said to have descended from the sky, became the soul of the Asante nation.
summary.zh: 奥塞·图图在登基拉和阿夸穆宫廷长大，与祭司奥孔福·阿诺基一起把库马西周围的阿肯酋邦联合为联盟，1701年在费亚塞摧毁登基拉的势力。据说从天而降的金凳成为阿散蒂民族的灵魂。

label.en: Killed in the war against Akyem
label.zh: 在对阿基姆的战争中阵亡

sources.title: Ivor Wilks, Asante in the Nineteenth Century (1975)
T. C. McCaskie, State and Society in Pre-Colonial Asante (1995)

note: Dates of birth, accession (c. 1680–1701) and death (1712–1717) vary between traditions; stops are approximate.

story.en:
According to Asante tradition, the young Osei Tutu was sent as a hostage to the court of Denkyira, the dominant Akan state, and later fled to Akwamu on the coast, where he met the priest Okomfo Anokye. When he returned to become king of Kumasi, he and Anokye set out to bind the neighbouring chiefdoms, all paying tribute to Denkyira, into a single nation.

The tradition says that at a great gathering Anokye called down from the sky a stool covered in gold, which came to rest on Osei Tutu’s knees. It contained, he declared, the sunsum, the spirit, of the whole Asante people; the chiefs buried their own stools of office and swore loyalty to it. No one, not even the king, may sit on the Golden Stool.

In 1701 the confederate army defeated Denkyira at Feyiase, and Asante took over its gold fields and its trade with the Europeans on the coast. Osei Tutu died in war against Akyem, killed, according to tradition, while crossing the Pra river; to this day Asante kings are said to avoid crossing it.
story.zh:
据阿散蒂传统，年轻的奥塞·图图被作为人质送到当时称霸的阿肯国家登基拉的宫廷，后来逃到沿海的阿夸穆，在那里结识祭司奥孔福·阿诺基。他回国成为库马西国王后，与阿诺基一起着手把向登基拉纳贡的周边各酋邦团结为一个民族。

传说在一次盛大集会上，阿诺基从天上召下一张镶金的凳子，它落在奥塞·图图的膝上。阿诺基宣布，凳中蕴藏着全体阿散蒂人的“松苏姆”（灵魂）；各酋长埋掉自己的权位之凳，宣誓效忠金凳。任何人，甚至国王，都不得坐在金凳上。

1701年联军在费亚塞击败登基拉，阿散蒂接管了其金矿以及与海岸欧洲人的贸易。奥塞·图图死于对阿基姆的战争，据传是在渡普拉河时被杀；据说直到今天，阿散蒂国王仍避免渡过这条河。

summary.en: Agaja expanded Dahomey from the Abomey plateau to the sea, conquering Allada (1724) and Hueda with its port of Ouidah (1727), and organised its army and administration for the slave trade. Oyo’s cavalry forced him to accept tributary status from 1730.
summary.zh: 阿加贾把达荷美从阿波美高原扩展到海边，征服阿拉达（1724年）和拥有维达港的胡埃达（1727年），并为奴隶贸易组织军队和行政体系。奥约骑兵迫使他自1730年起接受藩属地位。

sources.title: Robin Law, The Slave Coast of West Africa, 1550–1750 (1991)

note: Birth year approximate.

role.en: Queen mother of Ejisu and war leader
role.zh: 埃吉苏王太后、抗英领袖

summary.en: Queen mother of Ejisu, Yaa Asantewaa rallied the Asante chiefs to war when the British governor demanded the Golden Stool in 1900. Her forces besieged the British fort at Kumasi for months. Captured in 1901, she died in exile in the Seychelles.
summary.zh: 雅·阿散蒂瓦是埃吉苏的王太后。1900年英国总督索要金凳时，她号召阿散蒂酋长们开战，其部队围困库马西的英国堡垒数月。1901年她被俘，后在塞舌尔流放中去世。

label.en: Queen mother of Ejisu as the Asantehene is exiled
label.zh: 阿散蒂赫内被流放时任埃吉苏王太后

label.en: Leads the siege of the British fort at Kumasi
label.zh: 领导围攻库马西英国堡垒

sources.title: A. Adu Boahen, Yaa Asantewaa and the Asante–British War of 1900–1 (2003)

note: Her birth year is uncertain (c. 1840–1860).

story.en:
In 1896 the British exiled the Asantehene Prempeh I and other leaders, among them Yaa Asantewaa’s grandson, the chief of Ejisu. Four years later, on 28 March 1900, the governor of the Gold Coast, Sir Frederick Hodgson, addressed the chiefs in Kumasi and demanded to know where the Golden Stool was, so that he could sit on it as the representative of the queen. For the Asante, whose nation’s soul resided in the stool, this was sacrilege.

At a secret meeting that night, according to the account preserved in Asante memory, the chiefs hesitated, and Yaa Asantewaa, then perhaps sixty, shamed them: if the men of Asante would not fight, the women would. She was chosen as war leader. Within days Asante forces had trapped Hodgson, his wife and the garrison in the small fort at Kumasi.

The siege lasted until relief columns broke through in July, and the fighting continued until early 1901. Yaa Asantewaa was captured and deported to the Seychelles, where she died in 1921. The British annexed Asante, but they never got the stool, which had been hidden; in Ghana she remains a national heroine.
story.zh:
1896年，英国人流放了阿散蒂赫内普伦佩一世和其他首领，其中包括雅·阿散蒂瓦的孙子、埃吉苏的酋长。四年后的1900年3月28日，黄金海岸总督弗雷德里克·霍奇森爵士在库马西对酋长们讲话，要求知道金凳的下落，以便他作为女王的代表坐上去。对于民族之魂寄于金凳的阿散蒂人来说，这是亵渎。

据阿散蒂人保存的记忆，当晚的秘密会议上酋长们犹豫不决，当时约六十岁的雅·阿散蒂瓦羞辱他们说：如果阿散蒂的男人不愿战斗，女人们会去战斗。她被推举为战争首领。几天之内，阿散蒂军队就把霍奇森夫妇和守军困在库马西的小堡垒中。

围困一直持续到7月援军突破，战斗延续到1901年初。雅·阿散蒂瓦被俘，被流放到塞舌尔，1921年死于该地。英国吞并了阿散蒂，却始终没有得到被藏起来的金凳；在加纳，她至今是民族英雄。

summary.en: Born Kassa Hailu on the western frontier, Tewodros rose from bandit chief to emperor in 1855, ending the Era of the Princes. He tried to build a centralised state, a standing army and an arsenal, but his growing violence alienated his subjects, and he killed himself when a British army stormed Magdala in 1868.
summary.zh: 特沃德罗斯原名卡萨·海卢，出身西部边地，从绿林首领崛起，1855年称帝，结束了王子时代。他试图建立中央集权国家、常备军和兵工厂，但日益加剧的暴虐使臣民离心；1868年英军攻破马格达拉时他自杀身亡。

label.en: Born in Qwara on the western frontier
Fights the Egyptians at Debarki/Metemma frontier

label.zh: 在德拉斯格加冕为皇帝

label.en: Court and arsenal at Debre Tabor and Gafat
label.zh: 在德卜雷塔博尔和加法特设宫廷与兵工厂

sources.title: Sven Rubenson, King of Kings: Tewodros of Ethiopia (1966)

note: The 1848 frontier stop is approximate (his defeat by Egyptian forces near Dabaki).

name.zh: 穆罕默德·艾哈迈德（马赫迪）

role.en: Sufi leader and founder of the Mahdist state
role.zh: 苏菲派领袖、马赫迪国创建者

summary.en: A Sufi ascetic from a boat-building family of Dongola, Muhammad Ahmad proclaimed himself the Mahdi in 1881 and led a revolt against Turco-Egyptian rule. His followers destroyed an Egyptian army under Hicks Pasha in 1883 and took Khartoum in January 1885; he died months later in Omdurman.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德·艾哈迈德是出身栋古拉造船世家的苏菲派苦修者，1881年自称马赫迪，领导反抗土耳其-埃及统治的起义。其追随者于1883年歼灭希克斯帕夏率领的埃及军队，1885年1月攻占喀土穆；数月后他在恩图曼去世。

label.en: Born on Labab island near Dongola
label.zh: 生于栋古拉附近的拉巴卜岛

label.en: Settles as a Sufi teacher on Aba Island
label.zh: 在阿巴岛定居传授苏菲之道

label.en: Withdraws to Jebel Qadir in the Nuba Mountains
label.zh: 退至努巴山区的卡迪尔山

label.en: Takes El Obeid; destroys Hicks’s army at Shaykan
label.zh: 攻占欧拜伊德；在谢坎歼灭希克斯军队

sources.title: P. M. Holt, The Mahdist State in the Sudan, 1881–1898 (2nd ed., 1970)

story.en:
Muhammad Ahmad grew up in a family of boat-builders on the Nile and became a disciple of the Sammaniyya Sufi order, famous for his asceticism; he once broke with his own teacher for holding a lavish feast. On Aba Island in the White Nile he gathered followers who resented the taxes, corruption and foreign Christian officials of the Turco-Egyptian government in Khartoum.

In June 1881 he declared that he was the Mahdi, the guided one expected at the end of time. Two small expeditions sent to arrest him were wiped out by men armed mostly with spears, and he made a hijra, as the Prophet had, to Jebel Qadir. The victories brought in Baggara cattle nomads and whole regions. In November 1883 his forces encircled and destroyed an Egyptian army of some 8,000 men under the British officer William Hicks at Shaykan.

Britain sent Charles Gordon to evacuate Khartoum; instead he held on. The Mahdists stormed the city on 26 January 1885 and killed Gordon, two days before a British relief column arrived. The Mahdi died, probably of typhus, five months later, and his successor, the Khalifa ʿAbdallahi, ruled the Sudan for thirteen years.
story.zh:
穆罕默德·艾哈迈德生长于尼罗河畔的造船世家，成为萨曼尼耶苏菲教团的弟子，以苦修闻名；他曾因自己的老师大摆宴席而与之决裂。在白尼罗河上的阿巴岛，他聚集了一批不满喀土穆土耳其-埃及政府的苛税、腐败和外国基督徒官员的追随者。

1881年6月，他宣布自己是马赫迪，即末世降临的“受引导者”。两支前来逮捕他的小部队被主要手持长矛的人们全歼，他效仿先知迁徙到卡迪尔山。胜利吸引了巴加拉养牛游牧民乃至整片地区归附。1883年11月，他的军队在谢坎包围并歼灭了英国军官威廉·希克斯率领的约八千人的埃及军队。

英国派查尔斯·戈登去撤离喀土穆，他却坚守不走。1885年1月26日马赫迪军攻破该城，杀死戈登，两天后英国援军才赶到。五个月后马赫迪可能死于斑疹伤寒，继任者哈里发阿卜杜拉希统治苏丹十三年。

name.zh: 蒂普·蒂普（哈马德·本·穆罕默德·穆尔杰比）

role.en: Swahili-Arab ivory and slave trader, governor for the Congo Free State
role.zh: 斯瓦希里-阿拉伯象牙与奴隶商人、刚果自由邦总督

summary.en: The most powerful trader of the 19th-century East African interior, Tippu Tip built a commercial empire in the eastern Congo on ivory and captives, helped Livingstone, Stanley and Cameron, and in 1887 became Leopold II’s governor of the Stanley Falls district. His memoir, written in Swahili, is a major source for the period.
summary.zh: 蒂普·蒂普是19世纪东非内陆最有权势的商人，靠象牙和俘虏在刚果东部建立起商业帝国，曾帮助利文斯敦、斯坦利和卡梅伦，1887年成为利奥波德二世治下的斯坦利瀑布区总督。他用斯瓦希里语写成的回忆录是研究这一时期的重要史料。

label.en: Trading in Kazembe’s country near Lake Mweru; meets Livingstone
label.zh: 在姆韦鲁湖附近的卡曾贝领地经商；结识利文斯敦
在马涅马的卡松戈立足统治

label.en: Escorts Stanley from Nyangwe down the Lualaba
label.zh: 护送斯坦利从尼扬圭沿卢阿拉巴河而下

label.en: Governor of the Stanley Falls district

sources.title: Hamed bin Muhammed el Murjebi, Maisha ya Hamed bin Muhammed el Murjebi yaani Tippu Tip, trans. W. H. Whiteley (1958–59)
François Bontinck, L’autobiographie de Hamed ben Mohammed el-Murjebi Tippo Tip (1974)

note: Britannica gives 1837; other sources give 1832–1840, estimated from the ages he reported.

story.en:
Hamad bin Muhammad was born in Zanzibar to a family of Omani and Swahili traders and was trading inland by his late teens. His nickname is usually explained by the sound of his guns or by a nervous blink. In the 1860s he led caravans of hundreds of armed porters beyond Lake Tanganyika, where he won a reputation for audacity by seizing the stores of the chief Nsama in what is now Zambia.

By the 1870s he controlled a vast area of the upper Congo from Kasongo, where his plantations fed his followers and his agents raided for ivory and captives. European explorers depended on him: he met Livingstone, supplied Cameron and in 1876 escorted Stanley’s expedition down the Lualaba, the journey that showed it was the Congo, not the Nile.

In 1887 Stanley, now working for Leopold II, persuaded him to become the Free State’s governor at Stanley Falls. The arrangement collapsed within a few years in the Congo–Arab war. Tippu Tip retired to Zanzibar, rich, and dictated his memoirs in Swahili, a rare African view of the age of exploration and of the violence he himself had spread.
story.zh:
哈马德·本·穆罕默德生于桑给巴尔一个阿曼与斯瓦希里商人家庭，十几岁就已深入内陆经商。他的绰号通常被解释为源于枪声或他紧张时的眨眼。1860年代，他带领由数百名武装挑夫组成的商队越过坦噶尼喀湖，在今赞比亚境内夺取首领恩萨马的库存，以胆大闻名。

到1870年代，他从卡松戈控制着刚果上游的广大地区，种植园养活他的部众，手下四处劫掠象牙和俘虏。欧洲探险家依赖于他：他结识利文斯敦，为卡梅伦提供补给，1876年护送斯坦利的探险队沿卢阿拉巴河而下，这次旅程证明卢阿拉巴河是刚果河而非尼罗河的源流。

1887年，已为利奥波德二世效力的斯坦利说服他出任自由邦的斯坦利瀑布区总督。几年后在刚果-阿拉伯战争中这一安排瓦解。蒂普·蒂普富裕地退居桑给巴尔，用斯瓦希里语口述回忆录，这是关于探险时代以及他本人所散布之暴力的罕见非洲视角。

role.zh: 莱索托的创建者与国王

summary.en: A Koena chief, Moshoeshoe gathered refugees from the wars of the Mfecane on the flat-topped mountain of Thaba Bosiu and forged them into the Basotho nation. Through diplomacy, missionaries and war against the Orange Free State he preserved its core, placing it under British protection in 1868.
summary.zh: 莫舒舒是科埃纳部落的首领，在平顶山塔巴博休聚集姆菲卡尼战乱中的难民，把他们锻造成巴索托民族。他依靠外交、传教士以及与奥兰治自由邦的战争保住了国家的核心地区，并于1868年使其接受英国保护。

label.en: Moves his people to Thaba Bosiu

label.zh: 在莫里贾接纳法国传教士
巴苏陀兰成为英国保护地

sources.title: Leonard Thompson, Survival in Two Worlds: Moshoeshoe of Lesotho, 1786–1870 (1975)

note: Birth year approximate (c. 1786).

story.en:
In the 1820s the highveld was in turmoil, as raids, migrations and famine displaced whole communities in the period later called the Mfecane or Difaqane. Moshoeshoe, a young chief at Butha-Buthe, moved his followers in 1824 to Thaba Bosiu, a sandstone mountain with a flat summit, springs and grazing, reachable only by a few steep passes. Attackers repeatedly failed to take it.

He built his nation by taking in refugees of many origins and by generosity to defeated enemies. Tradition tells that when a band of cannibals who had eaten his grandfather came to him starving, he gave them cattle instead of revenge, saying that they were the living graves of his ancestor. He invited French Protestant missionaries in 1833, using them as advisers and go-betweens, though he never converted.

When Afrikaner settlers of the Orange Free State pushed onto his best farmland in the 1850s and 1860s, Moshoeshoe fought and negotiated, and finally asked Britain for protection, granted in 1868. He lost the fertile lowlands west of the Caledon, but Lesotho survived as the only kingdom inside South Africa, independent since 1966.
story.zh:
1820年代，南非高原陷入动荡，劫掠、迁徙和饥荒使整个社群流离失所，这一时期后来被称为“姆菲卡尼”或“迪法卡内”。布塔-布特的年轻首领莫舒舒于1824年带领追随者迁往塔巴博休，这是一座平顶砂岩山，有泉水和牧场，只有几条陡峭的山道可以上去。进攻者屡攻不克。

他通过收容各种来历的难民和宽待战败的敌人来建立自己的民族。传说一群曾吃掉他祖父的食人者饥肠辘辘地来投奔他，他没有复仇，反而送给他们牛，说他们是自己祖先的活坟墓。1833年他邀请法国新教传教士前来，用他们作顾问和中间人，但他本人从未改宗。

1850至1860年代，奥兰治自由邦的阿非利卡定居者侵入他最好的农田，莫舒舒边战边谈，最终请求英国保护，1868年获准。他失去了卡利登河以西的肥沃低地，但莱索托作为南非境内唯一的王国存续下来，并于1966年独立。

summary.en: Samuel Maharero led the Herero uprising against German colonial rule in January 1904. After defeat at the Waterberg in August, he and survivors fled across the Omaheke desert to British Bechuanaland while General von Trotha’s extermination order turned the war into genocide. He died in exile and was buried at Okahandja.
summary.zh: 塞缪尔·马哈雷罗于1904年1月领导赫雷罗人起义反抗德国殖民统治。8月在沃特贝格战败后，他与幸存者穿越奥马赫克沙漠逃往英属贝专纳兰，而冯·特罗塔将军的灭绝令使这场战争变成了种族灭绝。他死于流亡地，后归葬奥卡汉贾。

label.zh: 在奥卡汉贾成为最高首领

label.en: Reaches Bechuanaland after crossing the Omaheke
label.zh: 穿越奥马赫克后抵达贝专纳兰
在塞罗韦附近的流亡中去世

sources.title: Jan-Bart Gewald, Herero Heroes: A Socio-Political History of the Herero of Namibia, 1890–1923 (1999)
David Olusoga and Casper W. Erichsen, The Kaiser’s Holocaust (2010)

note: His first stop (1890) marks his accession; he was born at Okahandja in 1856.

summary.en: Crowned at 22 in 1883, Ranavalona III reigned while her prime minister and husband Rainilaiarivony held power, and lost the kingdom to the French invasion of 1895. Deposed in 1897, she was exiled to Réunion and then Algiers, where she died; her remains were returned to Antananarivo in 1938.
summary.zh: 拉纳瓦洛娜三世1883年22岁时加冕，在位期间实权由首相兼丈夫拉尼莱亚里沃尼掌握，1895年法国入侵后失去王国。1897年被废黜，先后流放留尼汪和阿尔及尔，在阿尔及尔去世；1938年遗骸被送回塔那那利佛。

label.en: Crowned at the Rova of Antananarivo
label.zh: 在塔那那利佛王宫加冕

sources.title: Stephen Ellis, The Rising of the Red Shawls (1985)

role.en: Educator, women’s rights campaigner and nationalist
role.zh: 教育家、妇女权利活动家、民族主义者

summary.en: The first girl to attend Abeokuta Grammar School, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti organised market women in the Abeokuta Women’s Union, whose tax protests forced the Alake of Egba into exile in 1948–49. A leader of Nigeria’s independence movement, she was the mother of the musician Fela Kuti.

sources.title: Cheryl Johnson-Odim and Nina Emma Mba, For Women and the Nation: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti of Nigeria (1997)

story.en:
Frances Abigail Olufunmilayo Thomas grew up in a Christian Egba family in Abeokuta, studied in England and came home to teach. Married to the clergyman and educator Israel Ransome-Kuti, she began in the 1940s by teaching literacy to market women and discovered their grievances: colonial taxes levied on women, price controls and seizures of rice, and the Alake, the Egba king, who collected the taxes for the British.

The Abeokuta Women’s Union, formed in 1946, claimed tens of thousands of members. Its protests in 1947 brought thousands of women to camp outside the Alake’s palace for days, singing songs that mocked him. In January 1949 the Alake, Ademola II, left the town and abdicated; the tax on women was abolished. She went on to campaign for women’s suffrage across Nigeria and travelled to the Soviet bloc and China.

In February 1977 soldiers raided the Lagos compound of her son, the Afrobeat musician Fela Kuti, which he called the Kalakuta Republic. She was thrown from an upstairs window and died of her injuries the next year. Fela delivered a mock coffin to the barracks of the head of state in protest.
story.zh:
弗朗西丝·阿比盖尔·奥卢芬米拉约·托马斯生长于阿贝奥库塔一个信奉基督教的埃格巴家庭，曾在英国求学，回国后任教。她嫁给牧师兼教育家伊斯雷尔·兰瑟姆-库蒂，1940年代开始教市场妇女识字，从而了解到她们的不满：对妇女征收的殖民税、价格管制和大米没收，以及替英国人收税的埃格巴国王阿拉凯。

1946年成立的阿贝奥库塔妇女联盟号称拥有数万会员。1947年的抗议使数千名妇女在阿拉凯王宫外露宿数日，唱着嘲讽他的歌。1949年1月，阿拉凯阿德莫拉二世离城退位，对妇女的征税被废除。她继而在尼日利亚全国争取妇女选举权，并访问了苏联阵营国家和中国。

1977年2月，士兵突袭她儿子、非洲节拍音乐家费拉·库蒂在拉各斯的住所，他称之为“卡拉库塔共和国”。她被从楼上窗口扔下，次年伤重去世。费拉把一口假棺材送到国家元首所在的军营以示抗议。

summary.en: A teacher called Mwalimu, Nyerere founded TANU in 1954, led Tanganyika to independence in 1961 and united it with Zanzibar as Tanzania in 1964. His Arusha Declaration launched ujamaa socialism; it failed economically, but Swahili-based nation-building gave Tanzania unusual stability. He stepped down voluntarily in 1985.

summary.en: Achebe’s Things Fall Apart (1958) and the novels that followed told the story of colonialism and independence from an Igbo point of view and helped create modern African literature in English. A Biafran envoy during the civil war, he later taught at Nsukka, Bard College and Brown University and was a sharp critic of Conrad’s Heart of Darkness.

summary.en: “Mama Africa” rose to fame in Johannesburg, went abroad in 1959 and was barred from returning after the Sharpeville massacre. She won a Grammy with Harry Belafonte, testified against apartheid at the United Nations and, after marrying Stokely Carmichael, lived in Guinea. She returned home in 1990 at Mandela’s invitation.

story.en:
Zenzile Miriam Makeba was born in a Johannesburg township in 1932 and, as she later told it, spent her first months in prison with her mother, who had been jailed for brewing beer. She sang with the Manhattan Brothers and the Skylarks in the 1950s and appeared in Lionel Rogosin’s anti-apartheid film Come Back, Africa, which took her to the Venice Film Festival in 1959.

She never returned home under apartheid. When she tried to go back for her mother’s funeral in 1960, after Sharpeville, her passport was cancelled. In New York Harry Belafonte promoted her, and songs such as “Pata Pata” and the Xhosa “Click Song” made her famous. In 1963 she testified at the United Nations, and South Africa banned her records.

Her marriage in 1968 to the Black Power leader Stokely Carmichael cost her American bookings, and they moved to Guinea, where Sékou Touré made her a diplomat. She sang at African independence celebrations across the continent. In 1990 Mandela, newly released, asked her to come home. She died in 2008 in Italy, shortly after singing at a concert against the Camorra.
story.zh:
曾济勒·米丽娅姆·马凯巴1932年生于约翰内斯堡的一个黑人城镇。据她后来讲述，她出生后的头几个月是和因酿啤酒入狱的母亲一起在监狱度过的。1950年代她与曼哈顿兄弟合唱团和云雀合唱团演唱，并出演了莱昂内尔·罗戈辛的反种族隔离电影《回来吧，非洲》，1959年随片前往威尼斯电影节。

在种族隔离时期她再也没能回家。1960年沙佩维尔惨案后，她想回国参加母亲的葬礼，护照却被注销。在纽约，哈里·贝拉方特力推她，《啪嗒啪嗒》和科萨语的《咔嗒歌》等歌曲使她成名。1963年她在联合国作证，南非随即禁售她的唱片。

1968年她与黑人权力运动领袖斯托克利·卡迈克尔结婚，失去了在美国的演出机会，两人移居几内亚，塞古·杜尔任命她为外交官。她在非洲各地的独立庆典上演唱。1990年刚获释的曼德拉邀请她回国。2008年她在意大利一场反对卡莫拉黑手党的音乐会上演唱后不久去世。

summary.en: An army captain who seized power in Upper Volta in 1983, Sankara renamed it Burkina Faso, “land of upright people”, and launched mass vaccination, literacy and tree-planting campaigns, banned female genital cutting and forced marriage, and cut the privileges of officials. He was killed in the coup of 1987 that brought Blaise Compaoré to power.

story.en:
Thomas Sankara was a guitar-playing army officer who had watched a popular revolt in Madagascar while training there in the early 1970s. Briefly prime minister in 1983, he was arrested, and his friend Captain Blaise Compaoré led the commandos of Pô to free him and seize power on 4 August 1983. He was 33.

He set out to make one of the world’s poorest countries self-reliant. In a few weeks in 1984 some two million children were vaccinated against measles, meningitis and yellow fever. Villages built schools and clinics; millions of trees were planted against the advancing Sahel. He sold the government’s fleet of Mercedes and made the Renault 5 the official car, and he spoke out against foreign debt at the OAU in 1987. His revolutionary tribunals and the banning of unions also made enemies.

On 15 October 1987 soldiers loyal to Compaoré shot Sankara and twelve aides at a meeting in Ouagadougou. Compaoré ruled for 27 years. In 2022 a military court in Burkina Faso convicted him in absentia of complicity in the murder.
story.zh:
托马斯·桑卡拉是一位会弹吉他的军官，1970年代初在马达加斯加受训时目睹了那里的民众起义。1983年他短暂出任总理后被捕，他的朋友布莱斯·孔波雷上尉率波城突击队营救他，并于1983年8月4日夺取政权。那年他33岁。

他决心让这个世界最贫穷的国家之一自力更生。1984年短短几周内，约两百万儿童接种了麻疹、脑膜炎和黄热病疫苗。村庄自建学校和诊所；数百万棵树被种下以抵御萨赫勒沙漠的扩张。他卖掉政府的奔驰车队，把雷诺5定为公务用车，1987年在非统组织会议上抨击外债。他的革命法庭和对工会的禁令也树敌不少。

1987年10月15日，效忠孔波雷的士兵在瓦加杜古的一次会议上枪杀了桑卡拉和十二名助手。孔波雷此后统治了27年。2022年，布基纳法索军事法庭缺席判定他是谋杀案的共犯。

summary.en: A teacher turned priest, Tutu became the first Black Anglican dean of Johannesburg, general secretary of the South African Council of Churches and, in 1986, Archbishop of Cape Town. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984 for non-violent opposition to apartheid, chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and coined the phrase “Rainbow Nation”.
